Sam RinzelSam Rinzel has 12 points in his last 10 games, all assists, including nine over a four-game point streak, and his ice time has jumped by more than two minutes to over 19 a night. The Athletic's Scott Powers put it simply: Rinzel "definitely seems like he has a confidence with the puck that he lost over last season."

The production is ahead of the process. He's at 2.2 points per 60 minutes, while our talent range puts his true rate closer to 1.0 to 1.6, and the Blackhawks have scored about six more goals than expected with him on the ice. The role is real, though: he's on the top power-play unit with Frank Nazar and Patrick Kane, and seven of his 14 points have come with the man advantage.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking liked his offensive instincts last season: he carried the puck in on 47% of his entries and got to the slot often for a defenseman. For a 25th overall pick, 0.67 points a game through 21 is far ahead of the 0.23 median for his draft range. The assist pace looks hot; the job looks real.
headline: Sam Rinzel has found the puck again
